capability: Merchant account and store owner (Shopify Account, Store Owner; Salla Your profile / الملف الشخصي, Merchant)
note: The merchant's own account on the platform and the person who owns the store. Shopify holds it mostly in its Terms of Service (Account Terms, Store Owner) and the account's store list; Salla in its profile settings, its Merchant API folder and the store.owner.changed event (M-002). Sign-in security (Shopify SH-C-007, Salla's two-factor and biometric flags) is the TRU batch's.

capability: The merchant agreement's contracting party and governing law (Shopify Contracting Party; Salla's owning company, شركة منصة سلة للاتصالات وتقنية المعلومات / شركة تطبيق سلة لتقنية المعلومات, شركة سلة القابضة)
note: The legal entity of the platform's group that is party to the merchant's agreement, and the law that governs it (M-001). Shopify chooses the entity by the store's billing address; Salla's held statements name its company in partner, app-store, theme-store, affiliate, campaign and migration terms, not in the merchant usage agreement (اتفاقية الاستخدام, SA-C-170), which batch 2 lands.

capability: Several stores under one owner (Shopify Organization and its stores; Salla Manage stores / إدارة المتاجر, قائمة المتاجر المرتبطة)
note: Joined on role (U-009): both group several stores under one owner's account and let the owner move between them. Shopify's organization also carries organization-scoped settings (Users, Billing) that Salla's linked-stores list doesn't show.

capability: Business entity a store operates as (Shopify Business entity: Individual, Company, Non-Profit; Salla الكيان القانوني / نوع الكيان)
note: The registered business or individual behind a store. Shopify keeps business entities in Organization settings and in General; Salla's statements are steps of its store verification (SA-C-006, domain C, names A under also). No shared grouping puts it under another capability, so it has no parent.

capability: Selling with multiple business entities from one store (Shopify Selling with multiple entities)
note: Several business entities, each with its own Shopify Payments account, assigned to markets. Shopify's own route business-entities/:businessEntityId sits under Payments, and its help names the entities of CM-ACC-004.

capability: Store details and general settings (Shopify General, Store properties; Salla General / عام, Settings)
note: The store's own general settings page and its API (M-006): Shopify Settings > General; Salla Settings > General with Store activity and Maintenance mode beneath it.

capability: Maintenance mode (Salla Maintenance mode / وضع صيانة المتجر)
note: Salla gives it its own route under General (general/maintenance-mode) and a plan line. Shopify's statements hold no maintenance or password-page setting (see its cell).

capability: Countries where the platform offers its service (Salla Available in / مدعوم في; Shopify Unsupported countries and regions)
note: Joined on role: Salla states the markets it serves; Shopify states the countries and regions it doesn't support. Shopify's sanctions concern (SH-C-174) and its sign-up location (SH-C-006) are the TRU and ONB batches' to land. Homonym (Q1's U-034, "supported countries"): WooCommerce's WooPayments supported countries (WC-C-010) are the countries of a payment service, not of the platform; the Shopify statements cited here are the platform-wide ones, not Shopify Payments' sanctions clauses (SH-S-0122, SH-S-0131).

capability: Staff accounts: the people other than the owner who work in the store's admin (Shopify Users, Staff Accounts; Salla Staff members, Employees / حسابات الموظفين)
note: Both platforms give it a settings route of its own (Shopify Users; Salla Staff members, /users), a plan line and an API (Shopify read_users, StaffMember; Salla Employees). Grain (M-004): Shopify splits staff accounts (SH-C-009) from roles and permissions (SH-C-010); Salla keeps both in SA-C-009, which lands here as the coarser concern. Its children are roles and permissions, user groups and staff targets, each with a route under this one.

capability: Roles and permissions of staff (Shopify Roles, permissions; Salla Roles & permissions / إدارة الأدوار الوظيفية)
note: Parent CM-STF-001: both platforms route roles under staff accounts (Shopify settings:organizations:accounts:roles; Salla /users/roles). The platform's permission system itself: the permissions each other capability cites are evidence for those capabilities, not here.

capability: User groups: staff grouped to receive roles together (Shopify Custom user groups)
note: Shopify gives it a route (settings:organizations:accounts:groups) and a plan line (Custom user groups, Plus). Parent CM-STF-001 by that route. Salla's statements hold none; Salla's Customer groups are buyers' groups, domain D's (CM-CUS-002), not this.

capability: Staff targets (Salla Employees targets)
note: Salla gives it a route of its own under Staff members (/users/targets). Neither platform's held statements define it: Salla names it only by its link.

capability: Third-party access to the merchant's admin, requested and granted per store (Shopify Collaborator access, collaborators; Salla support access requests / طلبات الدخول للمساعدة)
note: Joined on role (U-010): a partner outside the store's staff requests access to the merchant's admin and the merchant grants and limits it. No parent: Shopify routes it under its users (settings:organizations:accounts:collaborator) and files its permission under USER_MANAGEMENT; Salla routes it under its manage pages (/manage/support-access), beside custom URLs, webhooks and migration, not under /users. The partner's own side (its account, its partner portal) is domain F's.

capability: Subscription plans: the plan a store subscribes to, with its tiers and prices (Shopify Plan: Basic, Grow, Advanced, Plus; Salla Store plan / باقة المتجر: basic, plus, pro, special)
note: What the platform sells the merchant and gates by (M-007). Shopify keeps it in Settings > Plan, the subscribe and pick-period routes, the Plus section and the ShopPlan API object; Salla in Settings > Store plan (/plan) and its plans flag. What each plan includes is part of this capability: each plan line or plan-scoped flag is evidence for the capability it names, in that capability's domain, and no platform gives entitlements as such a place apart from the plan (the notes, batch 3). The plan's children here: its term and renewal (CM-PLN-002) and the fee on sales it sets (CM-PLN-003). A free trial and the inactive and pending-termination states are the ONB batch's.

capability: Plan term and renewal: the subscription's billing period, its contract term and its renewal (Shopify Pay monthly / Pay yearly, Shopify Plus Terms, Switch to 3-year term, Renewals; Salla annual subscription / الاشتراك السنوي, automatic renewal / تجديد باقة المتجر تلقائياً)
note: Shopify gives the Plus contract and its renewals a place of their own (plus/renew, plus/terms, the contractmanagement operations, SH-C-201) and the period a route (subscription/pick_period/:plan/:period); Salla states the annual subscription's freeze as a plan line and the plan's automatic renewal from the store balance.

capability: Platform fee on the merchant's sales, set by plan (Shopify Third-party transaction fees; Salla platform commission on sales / عمولة منصة على مبيعاتك)
note: A fee the platform takes on the value of the merchant's sales, varying by plan. Shopify's applies only to orders through payment providers other than Shopify Payments and shows on the bill (settings/billing) as well as in the plan table; both platforms show it as a plan line, so it sits under the plan. Payment processing fees are domain C's.

capability: Platform billing: the platform's charges to the merchant, its bills and invoices (Shopify Billing, Shopify bills; Salla Balance & billing / الرصيد والفواتير, إعدادات الفوترة)
note: How the platform bills the merchant (M-008): the billing section, the list of charges and invoices, the billing currency, and who may see them. App charges billed through the platform are domain F's (CM-APP-003); partner billing is F's (CM-PTN-004).

capability: Paying the platform's bills: the means the platform charges for its fees (Shopify billing payment methods, Authorized Payment Method, Pay bills; Salla the store balance that renews the plan, iTunes balance in Salla's iOS app / رصيد آيتونز)
note: Joined on role (reading): what the merchant's bills are paid from. Shopify charges a payment method the merchant keeps on file; Salla draws on the prepaid store balance (CM-PLN-006), and its سلة بلس plan line lets the subscription be managed in its iOS app with iTunes balance.

capability: Prepaid store balance with the platform: topped up, spent on the platform's services and withdrawn (Salla Store balance / رصيد المتجر, Wallet / محفظة المتجر)
note: Salla's balance, held apart from the e-payments balance (SA-S-0091), which is domain C's. Salla's own plan-feature grouping puts it with billing (the heading محفظة المتجر والفوترة, SA-I-1061), and Settings links Balance & billing as one page. Homonym: Shopify Balance (SH-C-088, domain C) is a money account for the merchant's sales, not a balance that pays Shopify.

capability: Taxes on the platform's own charges (Shopify Taxes on Shopify bills, Tax registration; Salla VAT on Salla's fees / ضريبة القيمة المضافة على إجمالي الرسوم)
note: Tax the platform adds to what it charges the merchant, not the merchant's sales tax (domain C). Q1's M-009 joins Shopify's SH-C-017 with WooCommerce's WC-C-057; Salla's statement sits in SA-C-113, domain C (U-029).

capability: Merchant's country at sign-up: the location the merchant gives when creating the store (Shopify I'm located in:, Country/region; Salla store country / دولة المتجر)
note: The country or region the merchant states on the sign-up or registration step. Shopify asks it on its sign-up page and requires the location to be kept current in the admin; Salla asks the store's country at registration, and says it decides the government documents the store is set up with. Joined on role (reading). Apart from CM-ACC-008, the countries where the platform offers its service: this is the one merchant's own location. Salla's SA-S-0141 is cited in both (see the notes, batch 4).

capability: Store status in its lifecycle: restricted access, suspension, inactivity, pending termination, reactivation and closure (Shopify store-unavailable, restricted access, inactive-account, pending-termination, reactivation, Term and Termination; Salla suspension of the store / إيقاف متجرك)
note: The states a store passes through when the platform restricts, suspends or terminates it or the merchant closes it, and the way back. Shopify places them in admin routes of their own (store-unavailable, inactive-account, pending-termination, reactivation) and in its Terms; Salla's held statement is only its violations page's warning that an uncorrected violation suspends the store. The violations and acceptable-use enforcement themselves are the TRU batch's (SH-C-172, SA-C-232). Homonym: domain G's CM-OPS-004 "Store status" is WooCommerce's system status report, not a store's lifecycle state.

capability: The platform's support and learning for merchants (Shopify 24/7 support, Shopify Academy, Shopify Learn, Shopify Community; Salla Help Center / مركز المساعدة - سلة, support plan, dedicated account manager / مدير حساب مخصص)
note: The help the platform's company gives its merchants: support by chat or an account manager, a help centre, courses and a community. Q1's M-066. Its level is set by plan on both (Shopify's 24/7 support row; Salla's سلة سبيشل lines). Homonym: SA-C-014's name carries "Self-service system", but Salla's Self-service system (نظام التذاكر) is the merchant's ticket system for its own customers, domain D's CM-SUP-005; no SA-C-014 statement holds it. Salla's support team's temporary access requests (SA-S-5132) are cited in CM-STF-005.

capability: Sign-in security for the admin: two-step authentication, passkeys and the sign-in methods of the platform's accounts (Shopify Security, two-step authentication, Sign in with passkey, External login services; Salla two-factor authentication / المصادقة الثنائية, نظام التحقق بخطوتين)
note: How the platform secures sign-in to the store's admin: a second step at sign-in, passkeys, sign-in with outside accounts, and for Shopify organizations MFA management, SAML and SCIM. Shopify places it in Settings > Security and the organization's accounts:security route; Salla states two-factor sign-in to its dashboard as mandatory (a help heading of SA-C-234, domain G with A under also) and holds two unreleased flags in its profile concern (SA-C-001). Joined on role (Q1's U-006: two-step against two-factor). No parent: Shopify's route sits under the organization's accounts (all users, not the owner's account alone) and Salla's two-step heading under platform security, so neither grouping puts it under CM-ACC-001 (reading). The buyers' sign-in is domain D's (CM-CUS-010 to CM-CUS-013).

capability: Identity verification of the people behind a store (Shopify Identity verification, Trust, Profile Assessment; Salla the store owner's identity checked through Absher / أبشر, and beneficial owners' data, in store verification)
note: The platform checks the identity of the store owner and of the people who own or run the business. Shopify gives it a route and admin sections of its own (profile-assessment, Trust, ProfileAssessment); Salla's held statements check the owner's identity and ask beneficial owners' data only as steps of its store verification (SA-C-006, domain C with A under also; the same statements are held under SA-C-232). Joined on role (Q1's U-007). The verification of the store's legal entity for payments, Shopify Payments' KYC (SH-C-068) and Salla's Store Verification, is domain C's.

capability: Audit log of admin activity (Shopify Merchant audit log, activity log, audit_events/admin_api_activity; Salla Activity history / سجل العمليات, audit_logs_management)
note: A record of the actions taken in the store's admin, by staff and through the API, for the merchant to review (Q1's M-005). Salla's Logs section (/logs) also holds the export log, which is domain G's CM-MIG-004. Homonym (Q1's U-044, "log"): WooCommerce's and BigCommerce's store logs, the entries a logger records, are domain G's CM-OPS-005, not this.

capability: Bot protection at checkout (Shopify Bot protection, CommerceProtection)
note: Shopify only so far: blocking known bots from the checkout and slowing bot activity, on Shopify Plus. Not reCAPTCHA at buyers' sign-in and registration, domain D's CM-CUS-012, nor API rate limits, domain F's (Q1's U-045: "rate limit" names an API limit on Shopify and Salla).

capability: Customers' personal data in the store: privacy settings, consent, data requests and erasure (Shopify Customer privacy, Privacy, Request data, Erase personal data; Salla customers' personal data under نظام حماية البيانات الشخصية, website-cookies, customer-data-export, customer-account-deletion)
note: Q1's M-059 at its coarser grain: Salla keeps cookies, data export and deletion in one concern (SA-C-066), Shopify splits privacy settings and consent (SH-C-148, CM-TRU-006) from data requests and erasure (SH-C-149, CM-TRU-007). This parent holds what the platforms state of the merchant's privacy duties as a whole. The data-protection roles (controller, processor: Shopify SH-C-180, Salla SA-C-171, Q1's M-060) are the next batches'. The store's privacy policy page is domain E's CM-CNT-008; the privacy compliance webhooks to apps domain F's CM-API-011.

capability: Privacy settings and cookie consent for the store's visitors (Shopify Customer privacy settings, Cookie banner, Customer Privacy API; Salla website-cookies, consent to the store's privacy policy at registration)
note: The store's privacy settings by region, its cookie consent banner, and the API that carries visitors' consent. Shopify places them in Settings > Customer privacy; Salla holds an unreleased flag and the consent notice at buyers' registration. Customers' marketing consent is domain D's CM-CUS-007.

capability: Customer data requests and erasure (Shopify Request data, Erase personal data; Salla customer-data-export, customer-account-deletion)
note: The merchant answers a customer's request for their personal data, or has it erased. Shopify places them as staff permissions in Customers and as access scopes; Salla holds two dashboard flags only, whose subject no statement states. The webhooks that pass these requests to apps are domain F's CM-API-011.

capability: The platform's own use of the store's customer data across merchants for its services, under the merchant's setting (Shopify: Shopify Network Intelligence, Enhanced Services)
note: Shopify only so far: Enhanced Services, powered by Shopify Network Intelligence, which lets Shopify use the store's customers' personal data with other merchants' for its own services, Shopify acting as controller; the merchant may turn the setting off. Its parent is CM-TRU-006 because Shopify places the setting in the Customer privacy settings (SH-S-6326). Salla's analysis of customers' data across its stores for a fraud tag and for cash on delivery (SA-S-5052, SA-S-0110) is a feature's input, cited in its own capabilities; see the notes, batch 5.

capability: Acceptable use and enforcement: the platform's rules on what merchants may do with it, reports of violations and the platform's action on them (Shopify Acceptable Use Policy, Report an issue with a merchant, Resolving terms violations; Salla Violations / المخالفات)
note: The rules the merchant must keep and how the platform enforces them. The store states that follow (restricted access, suspension, termination) are CM-ONB-002. Salla's usage policy (سياسة الاستخدام على منصة سلة, SA-C-170) isn't held as text. The businesses Shopify Payments prohibits are domain C's (SH-C-173).

capability: The merchant's legal compliance as the seller: responsibility for its goods and transactions, and the laws, licences and product rules it must keep (Shopify Your Responsibilities, Compliance, Product disclosures; Salla compliance with e-commerce laws / امتثالاً لقوانين التجارة الإلكترونية, شهادة توثيق التجارة الإلكترونية)
note: Q1's M-086 (Shopify with WooCommerce's WC-C-027). Shopify makes the merchant the seller, places guidance in its help's Compliance section and gives product disclosures for required warnings; Salla's held statements require the store's customer-service information and the Business platform's e-commerce certificate under its market's laws. Partners' licences are domain F's. Q1's U-039 (Salla's licences, SA-C-231) is batch 7's.

capability: Intellectual property infringement: reports of content that infringes others' rights, and the platform's action on it (Shopify Intellectual Property, copyright policy, trademark policy, Reporting copyright infringement; Salla حقوق الملكية الفكرية in the App Maker's publishing policy)
note: Under CM-TRU-009 because Shopify's Terms make infringing content a violation of its Acceptable Use Policy (SH-S-7260). The merchant's own licence of its Materials to Shopify (SH-S-0042) is held here as the Terms' section on rights in store content. Not Salla's store content protection (حماية محتوى المتجر, content-copyright: SA-S-2035, SA-S-3363, domain E's SA-C-090), which guards the store's own content from copying.

capability: Merchants' complaints to the platform about its own services (Shopify Internal Complaint-Handling System, Submit a P2B complaint, P2B Form, Submit a financial complaint)
note: The platform's own handling of complaints its merchants make about it: Shopify's internal complaint-handling system under its EU and UK platform-to-business terms, and its form for complaints about its financial products. Homonym (Q1's U-040): Salla's complaints platform (منصة الشكاوى, SA-C-178) holds buyers' complaints about stores, with Salla as mediator; domain D's CM-SUP-008 is the merchant handling its own customers' complaints; Salla's quality gateway (بوابة الجودة, SA-C-150, domain C) holds merchants' complaints about shipping companies. None is a complaint about the platform's own services.

capability: The platform's data protection terms: its privacy policy and data processing addendum, and who is controller and who processor of the personal data a store holds (Shopify Privacy Policy, Data Processing Addendum, Data Controller, Data Processor; Salla سياسة الخصوصية, جهة التحكم)
note: Q1's M-060 (SH-C-180 with Salla's privacy policy SA-C-171, batch 7's). The parent of the terms' parts that have a place of their own: where data is stored (CM-TRU-014), subprocessors (CM-TRU-015), retention after closure (CM-TRU-016) and legal requests (CM-TRU-017). Not under CM-TRU-005 (my judgment): the privacy policy and DPA cover the merchant's own data as well as its customers' (SH-S-0182, SH-S-0185). Shopify as controller for Enhanced Services is CM-TRU-008's subject; SH-S-0192 is cited in both.

capability: Where the platform stores and processes data: hosting locations and international transfers (Shopify Data hosting locations, Global Data Transfers, Binding Corporate Rules)
note: Under CM-TRU-013 because Shopify states it in its DPA (A. Global Data Transfers, SH-S-0188) and its privacy policy (Where we send your information, SH-S-0175). The infrastructure's reliability (pods, recovery sites: SH-S-0672, SH-S-0673, SH-S-0674) is domain G's CM-OPS-001; the hosting environment of a store is G's CM-OPS-003. Salla's side (SA-C-233, Q1's U-042) has no statement: every placement is 'page not read'.

capability: Subprocessors: the third parties and affiliates the platform engages to process data, its list and notice of changes (Shopify Subprocessors, Shopify affiliated subprocessors)
note: Under CM-TRU-013 because Shopify's DPA governs them (Appendix C, 4. Subprocessors, SH-S-0189, SH-S-0190). Not the sharing of a store's data with a payment provider the merchant connects (Salla's SA-S-0109, SA-S-5048, domain C; Q1's U-043).

capability: Retention and deletion of store data after the store closes (Shopify retain store information for two years)
note: Under CM-TRU-013 because Shopify states it in its privacy policy (How long we keep your information, SH-S-0182) and its DPA (SH-S-7290). The store's closure itself is CM-ONB-002; the webhook shop/redact and apps' deletion of a store's data after uninstall are domain F's CM-API-011. Not Salla's deleted orders and products (/orders/trash, /products/trash), items deleted within a live store.

capability: Legal requests for information: requests from third parties and public authorities for data the platform holds, and its rules for answering them (Shopify Legal Access Request form, guidelines for legal requests for information, Transparency Report)
note: Under CM-TRU-013 because Shopify's privacy policy states the rule (Our values, We protect your information from others, SH-S-0185). Not dispute resolution before courts (Salla's SA-S-0021).

capability: Payment card data security: the platform's PCI DSS compliance for the card data it handles for the store (Shopify PCI DSS, Account Data, Level 1 PCI DSS compliant)
note: Q1's M-062 (Shopify with WooCommerce's WC-C-018 and WC-C-019). Card data security only: payment processing is domain C's, and the P2PE service on POS equipment provided by Stripe (SH-S-0089) is domain E's CM-POS-002. SH-S-0097 is the same PCI DSS responsibility stated in the Shopify Payments terms; domain C's part should not cite it as core again. TLS on Salla's REST APIs (SA-S-0174) is API security, domain G's SA-C-234.

capability: Security and legal apps for the store (Shopify Security apps, Anti theft apps, Security - Other, Legal apps)
note: Shopify's App Store categories, held by their headings only: what the apps do isn't stated, so no capability of their subject is cited (CM-TRU-004, CM-TRU-006 or CM-TRU-010 might be). WooCommerce's Policy and security subcategory (Q1's U-064) is WooCommerce's part's.

capability: The platform's handling of buyers' complaints about stores, as mediator between buyer and merchant (Salla complaints platform / منصة الشكاوي, نظام الشكاوى)
note: Salla only so far: the customer opens a complaint on Salla's complaints system page (SA-S-5085), Salla's team reviews it first (SA-S-5088), Salla acts as link and mediator between the merchant and its customer (SA-S-5087), and only the customer closes it (SA-S-5086). Homonyms: CM-TRU-012 is merchants' complaints to the platform about its own services (Shopify's P2B and financial complaints); domain D's CM-SUP-008 is the store's complaints record the merchant manages (Salla Complaints, /manage/complaints, complaint_management); Salla's quality gateway (بوابة الجودة, SA-C-150, domain C) is merchants' complaints about shipping companies; Shopify's disputes are payment chargebacks. Kept apart from CM-SUP-008 as the coordinator's message for batch 7 directs, though CM-SUP-008's Zid cell (Zid handles complaints against stores, ZD-S-0998, ZD-S-0935) shows the same role: see the notes, batch 7.

capability: Site visibility before launch: the store's coming-soon mode and its launch (WooCommerce Site visibility, Coming soon mode, Launch your store)
note: Added by A-woocommerce, batch 1, for WC-C-082. Under CM-ACC-006 because WooCommerce's Site visibility is a section of its settings (WC-S-0009, inventory list settings, WC-I-0009), as Salla's maintenance mode is a route under General. Not joined with CM-ACC-007 (Salla Maintenance mode): Salla's held statements name maintenance mode (SA-S-1726, SA-S-2084) without saying what it does to the storefront, so no definition shows the same role; Q1's U-069 is ruled apart. The reviewer may join them on role if a definition of Salla's mode is held.

capability: Connecting the store to the platform company's account for its services (WooCommerce: WordPress.com account, Jetpack connection)
note: Added by A-woocommerce, batch 1, for WC-C-049. Not CM-APP-012 (domain F), the connection to WooCommerce.com for marketplace extensions: this is a WordPress.com account and the Jetpack connection that Automattic's services WooPayments, WooCommerce Tax and WooCommerce Shipping need (WC-S-5335, WC-S-0464). Not CM-ACC-001 either: the statements show a connection of the site for services, not the account the store is owned and signed into, which is WordPress's (reading).

capability: Licence of the platform's software, with its warranty (WooCommerce GPLv3, open-source)
note: Added by A-woocommerce, batch 1, for WC-C-025. The terms under which the merchant may run the platform's software. Kept apart from CM-ACC-002: the GPLv3 names no contracting party and no governing law, and WooCommerce's own readme gives it (WC-S-0589). Searched in every domain: no capability holds a software licence (caps: licence, license, GPL, open source).

capability: Store setup in the admin: the setup wizard, the merchant's onboarding profile and the setup tasks (WooCommerce Setup Wizard, onboarding profile, onboarding tasks)
note: Added by A-woocommerce, batch 1, for WC-C-081. Shopify's seed grouping names an onboarding question and home setup; no capability held it. Homonym: WooCommerce's inbox (admin notes, WC-S-0206) is not Shopify Inbox, chat with customers (CM-SUP-004).

capability: Store data sent from the merchant's own site to the platform company: usage tracking and data synced for its services (WooCommerce usage tracking, wc-telemetry; Jetpack Sync)
note: Added by A-woocommerce, batch 2, for WC-C-035 and WC-C-117. WooCommerce only so far: the software runs on the merchant's own site, and these are the flows of the store's data from it to Automattic. Usage tracking has a place of its own: the settings section Advanced > WooCommerce.com (WC-S-0027), its opt-in setting woocommerce_allow_tracking, off by default (WC-S-5370), and the REST namespace wc-telemetry (WC-S-0079); Jetpack Sync, Automattic's, caches the site's data, orders included, to WordPress.com servers as part of the required connection (WC-S-0953, WC-S-0955). Not CM-TRU-008: Shopify Network Intelligence is the platform's use of the store's customer data across merchants, while usage tracking sends the store's own settings and aggregate counts to improve WooCommerce (WC-S-0500, WC-S-0572), a reading. Not CM-ACC-010, the connection itself, nor domain G's CM-OPS-005 (Remote Logging, WC-C-036) or domain D's CM-ANL-001 (WooCommerce Analytics syncing, WC-C-039), which name other flows. `caps` on telemetry, usage tracking, sync, tracker found none.

capability: Products: the store's product catalog (Shopify Products; Salla Products / المنتجات)
note: Parent of CM-CAT-002 to CM-CAT-009 and CM-CAT-011: the product record and what the platforms keep on it. Both keep products as one admin section and one API group (M-011).

capability: Product options and variants (Shopify variants; Salla Product Options, Option Values, Variants)
note: Shopify keeps variants inside its products concern; Salla gives options and variants their own API folders, webhooks and plan line.

capability: Store product groupings: collections and categories (Shopify Collections; Salla Categories / الأقسام, تصنيفات المنتجات; WooCommerce Product categories)
note: The store's own groupings of its products. Joined on role: Shopify's collections and Salla's categories (landings, notes). Homonyms: WooCommerce's Store API collection-data route (WC-C-064/boundary/WC-S-0172) is not a grouping of products, and Shopify's 'product categories' of its tax statements (SH-C-100/decides/SH-S-7221) aren't the store's groupings (S12).

capability: Standard product taxonomy (Shopify taxonomy linking; Salla google-taxonomy, salla-taxonomy)
note: A standard classification of products, apart from the store's own groupings. Salla keeps it in its categories concern. Homonym: WordPress taxonomies (WC-C-064/where/WC-S-0907) are the mechanism of WooCommerce's categories and tags, not a standard classification (S12).

capability: Brands (Salla Brands / الماركات التجارية)
note: A product's brand as its own record. Salla and WooCommerce (Products > Brands) keep one; Shopify holds no brand statement.

capability: Product tags (Shopify product tags; Salla Product Tags / وسوم المنتجات)
note: Both keep tags inside their products concerns.

capability: Product media: images, video and 3D (Shopify media; Salla Product Images, media-center)
note: Both keep media inside their products concerns.

capability: Combined listings (Shopify Combined Listings)
note: 'A combined listing of products' (SH-S-7455), on Shopify's Plus plan. Shopify only so far.

capability: Product restrictions (Salla Product restrictions / قيود المنتج, sales-restrictions)
note: Salla only so far; its statements don't say what a restriction limits (notes). Homonym: WooPayments' prohibited product types (WC-C-011/decides/WC-S-0523) restrict what a merchant may sell with that payment service, not a product (S12).

capability: Product sourcing: dropshipping, print on demand and wholesale buying (Shopify sourcing apps; Salla Drop shipping apps and wholesale market)
note: Finding and sourcing products from others: Shopify's Finding products and Dropshipping apps and Shopify Collective's 'sell and source'; Salla's Drop shipping apps and its wholesale market's buying side. Shopify Collective, Shopify's own way to sell and source other stores' products, is E's CM-CHN-005, where its statements count; here they show (the coordinator, after E-anchor batch 4).

capability: Size guides (Salla size guides / جدول المقاسات)
note: Salla's size guides (جدول المقاسات), a permission and a feature of type app. Salla only so far.

capability: Subscriptions and recurring payments (Shopify subscriptions and selling plans; Salla Recurring Payments / subscriptions)
note: Recurring purchases a store sells to its customers (M-074).

capability: Digital products: downloadable files and digital codes (Shopify digital goods; Salla Digitals Product, digital codes and files; WooCommerce downloadable products)
note: Products delivered as files or codes (M-076). Parent of CM-SEL-003.

capability: NFTs and token-gating (Shopify Blockchain, nft-application)
note: Shopify only so far; Shopify keeps it with digital goods.

capability: Bookings and reservations (Salla Bookings, Order Reservations / الحجوزات; WooCommerce Bookings and appointments; Shopify Event booking apps)
note: Salla's booking product, kept apart from normal products (SA-S-5012); WooCommerce's Bookings and appointments land here by M-081, and Shopify's cell rests on its App Store category (C2). Homonym: Salla's Order Reservations are bookings, not stock held for an order (CM-INV-008).

capability: Pre-orders (Salla Pre-order campaigns / حملات الطلب المسبق; Shopify Pre-order apps)
note: Salla's pre-order campaigns; Shopify's cell rests on its App Store category (C2).

capability: Product bundles (Shopify bundles; Salla bundle products; WooCommerce Bundles, Product Bundles)
note: Salla's bundle products and Shopify's bundle apps, extension template and bundles scope.

capability: Donations (Shopify Donation apps; Salla Quick donation / التبرع السريع, product donation options)
note: Salla's quick donation and product donation options; Shopify's Donation apps (cited from domain D).

capability: Inventory tracking: stock quantities (Shopify Inventory; Salla Inventory, Product Quantity / إدارة المخزون)
note: Parent of CM-INV-002 to CM-INV-004, CM-INV-006 and CM-INV-007 (M-012). Shopify's inventory entitlement holds counts, purchaseOrders and transferLocation as siblings (SH-C-022/decides/SH-S-5334), which sets the tree (S2).

capability: Inventory history: the log of stock changes (Shopify inventory history; Salla Inventory log / سجل كميات المنتجات)
note: Both keep it inside their inventory concerns.

capability: Inventory counts and stocktakes (Shopify inventory counts; Salla جرد المنتجات والمخزون, Inventory audit)
note: Shopify gates it by its own entitlement; Salla names it by a plan line and a dashboard link (C3). What a count or a stocktake does isn't stated by either beyond its name.

capability: Low stock: alerts and lists (Salla product.quantity.low, product-quantity-notify; WooCommerce ProductsLowInStock)
note: Salla's alert to the store when a product's quantity is low; WooCommerce's is an API listing products low in stock (WC-C-068/boundary/WC-S-0219). Not the buyers' back-in-stock alerts (domain D).

capability: Inventory locations: locations, branches and warehouses (Shopify Locations; Salla Branches, Warehouses & branches / الفروع والمستودعات)
note: Where a store's stock is held, as a reading: joined on role (landings, notes).

capability: Inventory transfers and shipments (Shopify Transfers and inventory shipments; Salla Inventory transfer)
note: Under inventory by Shopify's own grouping: its inventory entitlement holds transferLocation beside counts and purchaseOrders (SH-S-5334). Salla's Inventory transfer link is a sibling of Inventory management and Warehouses & branches in one flat list under /products (SA-S-1797, SA-S-1798, SA-S-1808), and only Q1's concern SA-C-026 groups transfer with branches; the anchor platforms' admin grouping decides (S2). Parent of nothing: purchase orders are a sibling (CM-INV-007).

capability: Purchase orders and suppliers (Shopify Purchase orders, suppliers)
note: Shopify's purchase orders and the suppliers it keeps with them. Under inventory by Shopify's own grouping: the inventory entitlement holds purchaseOrders (SH-S-5334), and the purchase-order permission sits in the subcategory Inventory (SH-S-7156). Its permissions depend on the transfer permissions, which is not a part-of relation (S2). Shopify only so far.

capability: Product cost: cost of goods sold (WooCommerce Cost of Goods Sold, _cogs_value; Shopify View cost, Edit cost)
note: A product's cost, entered on the product ('Cost of goods', WC-S-5446) behind WooCommerce's cost_of_goods_sold feature (WC-S-5445). Shopify's cell cites its staff permissions to view and edit a product's cost, inventory entries Q1 placed in SH-C-020 with no statement (C2, after the dry run's review); no statement says where Shopify's cost is entered. Salla's profit analytics are domain D's.

capability: Memberships (WooCommerce Memberships)
note: A Marketplace category of WooCommerce's Merchandising group (WC-S-0728), its only statement. No statement says what a membership sells or whether it recurs, so it stays apart from subscriptions (CM-SEL-001). WooCommerce only so far.

capability: Stock held for unpaid orders (WooCommerce Hold stock)
note: Stock held for a pending order for a set number of minutes, after which the order is cancelled (WC-S-5401). WooCommerce only so far. Not Salla's Order Reservations, which are bookings (CM-SEL-004; the anchor's homonyms).

capability: Product pricing (Shopify Pricing apps; Salla Automatic pricing, product.price.updated; WooCommerce Pricing extensions)
note: Added after the dry run's review (S8): Salla gives it a setting of its own under products (products/products.auto_pricing, SA-S-1751) and a webhook, Shopify four App Store categories and WooCommerce a Marketplace category. No statement of any platform says what the pricing does: the platforms name it and never define it. Parent CM-CAT-001 by Salla's admin grouping, its products settings; Shopify's and WooCommerce's groupings put it only in their app stores (Merchandising, for WooCommerce). Homonyms: Shopify's 'pricing' plans (SH-C-015) and Shopify App Pricing (SH-C-019, an app's billing); Salla's shipping pricing (تسعيرة الشحن, SA-C-140, SA-C-142); a product's tax pricing (SA-C-160) and prices by exchange rate (SA-C-163, SH-C-108, WC-C-052), which are other domains'.

capability: Product badges (Zid Product Badge)
note: An API group of Zid's own, Merchant APIs > Products > Product Badge (ZD-I-0011, an inventory entry Q1 placed in ZD-C-083, which no statement covers). It is a place of its own (an API group, by the dry run's convention), so it is a capability; no statement says what a badge is or where it shows, so the capability rests on the name only, and a reviewer may fold it into CM-CAT-001. Zid only so far.

capability: Barcode printing (Zid Barcode Printing / طباعة الباركود)
note: A plan line of Zid's Product & Inventory Management group (ZD-I-0249, placed in ZD-C-083, which no statement covers). A place of its own (a plan line); no statement says what is printed or from where, so it rests on the name. Shopify's barcode permission (products:variants:update:barcodes, in CM-CAT-002) is about a variant's barcode value, not printing; the back-fill decides whether it is cited here. Zid only so far.

capability: Inventory withdrawal priority (Zid Inventory Withdrawal Priority / أولوية السحب من المخزون)
note: A plan line with its own description, 'Set inventory withdrawal priority to avoid stockouts and ensure quick order fulfillment.' (ZD-S-0919), and a help-center statement that it isn't in the free plans (ZD-S-1023). No statement says what the priority is set among; that it orders the stock locations an order draws from is a reading, not stated, so its parent is inventory tracking (CM-INV-001), not locations (CM-INV-005). Zid only so far.

capability: Products shown by the customer's city (Zid Display Products by Customer City / عرض المنتجات حسب مدينة العميل)
note: A plan line of Zid's Product & Inventory Management group (ZD-I-0257) that Q1 placed in Zid's inventory concern ZD-C-085, and a plan card that groups it with inventory counting and transfer, 'Inventory counting, transfer, and display by customer city' (ZD-I-0405). No statement says what decides which products a city sees; that it follows the stock at locations is a reading. A reviewer may move it to domain E (storefront) if a statement shows it is a display setting. Zid only so far.

capability: Checkout: the step in which the buyer completes the order (Shopify Checkout, Shopify's checkout settings; Salla Checkout / store-checkout, Guest checkout, Checkout APIs)
note: Parent of CM-CHK-002 to CM-CHK-004. Q1's M-021, a difference of grain: Shopify splits cart (SH-C-046) from checkout (SH-C-047); Salla keeps them in one concern (SA-C-100), which lands here, the coarser capability. Both platforms give checkout a place of its own: Shopify's settings page Checkout and its route checkout-settings (SH-S-1489, SH-S-5106); Salla's dashboard link Checkout at /checkout and its Merchant docs collection Checkout APIs (SA-S-1685, SA-S-1166). Salla's guest checkout (its settings page checkout/guest-checkout and the flag guest-checkout) stays here, under Salla's own checkout settings; WooCommerce's guest-checkout setting is cited in domain D's CM-CUS-010 (customer accounts), see notes. Shopify's Universal Commerce Protocol checkout (dev.ucp.shopping.checkout) is domain F's CM-AIA-005, agentic commerce.

capability: Cart: the buyer's cart before checkout (Shopify Cart, carts/create, Add-to-cart limit; Salla Cart, Cart Items in the Checkout APIs)
note: Under CM-CHK-001 by Salla's grouping: its Checkout APIs collection is "designed for developers building integrations that need to control cart and checkout-entry flows" (SA-S-5139), and its folders Cart and Cart Items sit in that collection (a reading: the collection's sidebar, read as context in observed-sa, not cited). Shopify's own grouping keeps Cart apart from Checkout (its Cart label and carts webhook topics, SH-S-0771, SH-S-6066), so the groupings differ and Salla's is followed, as the one that groups them (notes). The storefront's cart API as such is domain E's (CM-SFR-011, CM-SFR-012); this capability is the cart object and its rules.

capability: Checkout customization and branding: the merchant's editor and settings for the checkout's look and configuration (Shopify Checkout branding, Checkout and accounts configurations, checkout and accounts editor, Checkout customization)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-CHK-001 by Shopify's own route, settings/checkout/editor (SH-S-5103), inside its checkout settings. Shopify's editor configures the checkout and the customer accounts pages together (SH-S-5942); customer accounts themselves are domain D's CM-CUS-010.

capability: Checkout UI extensions: apps' blocks and pages in the checkout and the thank-you page (Shopify Checkout UI, Post-purchase UI, Checkout Extensibility)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-CHK-001 by Shopify's own words, "To augment Shopify checkout with new functionality, build an app with extensions" (SH-S-0679), and its legal heading 9.13 Shopify Checkout Extensibility, "use extensions to customize your checkout" (SH-S-0069). Q1's M-022 joins it to WooCommerce's WC-C-087, for the WooCommerce part. Like D's CM-CUS-014 (customer account UI extensions) and E's CM-POS-004 (POS extensions), the extension surface of one feature stays with the feature; apps as such are domain F's.

capability: Cart and checkout validation: app-written rules that block a cart or checkout from going ahead (Shopify Cart and Checkout Validation, a Shopify Function API)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. No parent: Shopify groups it among its Function APIs (SH-S-0853), not under its checkout or cart. Functions as such are domain F's CM-APP-005, whose note leaves the single features' function APIs to their domains. What a validation checks is not defined in a statement held, beyond its name.

capability: Cart transform: app-written logic that changes the lines of a cart (Shopify Cart Transform, cart transformer, a Shopify Function API)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. No parent: Shopify groups it among its Function APIs (SH-S-0854, SH-S-2225). What a transform does is not defined in a statement held beyond its name; one guide that requests its scope is a bundles guide (SH-S-6173's source page, read as context), which domain B's CM-SEL-006 holds as bundles, not this.

capability: Abandoned checkouts and abandoned carts: the store's records of checkouts and carts the buyer did not complete (Shopify Abandoned checkouts; Salla Abandoned Carts / السلات المتروكة)
note: Q1's unclear candidate U-001, ruled joined here: both platforms give the records a place of their own, Shopify's admin route at checkouts with the permission MANAGE_ABANDONED_CHECKOUTS (SH-S-5001, SH-S-5002), Salla's dashboard app at /marketing/carts and its Merchant API folder Abandoned Carts (SA-S-3591, SA-S-1035). The recovery, the messages and offers that bring the buyer back, is domain D's CM-MKT-022, which cites the recovery statements of the same concerns (SH-S-7224, SH-S-7041, SH-S-5277, SA-S-2099, SA-S-1814, SA-S-1191). Homonym kept in view: Shopify's checkout against Salla's cart, see notes. No parent: Shopify's staff permission puts it under Orders (Orders > Abandoned checkouts), Salla's link under marketing.

capability: Quick checkout: a button or link that shortens the buyer's way through checkout (Salla Quick checkout / زر الشراء السريع, الطلب المباشر, salla-quick-buy; Shopify accelerated checkout buttons)
note: A join on role, a reading: Salla's quick purchase "relies on reducing and speeding up the steps of completing the order" (SA-S-5027); Shopify's accelerated or express checkouts let "returning customers ... more quickly complete payment for their orders" (SH-S-7287), with buttons on Shopify Checkout (SH-S-0419). Shopify's statements are SH-C-078's (PAY batch 4), and Shop Pay (SH-C-074) is the other side of U-026: see notes. Salla's own lines name two things, the quick-buy button (زر الشراء السريع, quick-purchase, salla-quick-buy) and direct ordering (الطلب المباشر, quick-checkout, the route /marketing/quick_checkout); neither is defined apart, so they stay in one capability. No parent: Salla's grouping is marketing, Shopify's is its checkout.

capability: Order options and custom fields at checkout: options and fields the merchant adds for the buyer to fill in when ordering (Salla Cart options / خيارات الطلب, Order Options, Custom fields / حقول مخصصة للطلبات)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Salla's dashboard links Cart options (/orders/options) and Custom fields (/orders/custom-fields) sit in its Orders section (SA-S-1782, SA-S-1780). No parent here: Salla's grouping is its orders section, whose capabilities are batch 2's (ORD). Q1's unclear candidate U-005 sets Shopify's metafields (SH-C-028, domain E) against it: ruled apart. What a cart option is is not defined in a statement held. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping, convention 6: its links are /orders/options and /orders/custom-fields, in the same admin list as All orders (the coordinator, after batch 2).

capability: Orders: the store's orders and their management in the admin (Shopify Orders; Salla Orders / الطلبات, All orders)
note: Parent of CM-ORD-002 to CM-ORD-005, CM-ORD-007, CM-ORD-008 and CM-ORD-010 to CM-ORD-014. Q1's M-023, a difference of grain: Shopify keeps cancellation in orders and splits editing (SH-C-056); Salla splits statuses (SA-C-041) and cancellation (SA-C-046) and keeps editing, manual orders, tags, deleted orders, notes and reorder in SA-C-040. Both coarse concerns (SH-C-054, SA-C-040) land here, and each finer thing is a child. The children follow the platforms' shared grouping: Shopify's routes for editing and creating orders sit in its section Orders (SH-S-7095, SH-S-7094), and Salla's links and settings sit under its Orders section (/orders/...).

capability: Order editing: changing an order after it is placed, and the buyer's requests to edit it (Shopify Edit orders, order edits, requested order edits; Salla Order editing / تعديل الطلب)
note: Under CM-ORD-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route order:edit is in its section Orders (SH-S-7095); Salla's setting Order editing is orders/edit-policy (SA-S-1747). Q1's M-023 holds SH-C-056 with SA-C-040, which lands in the parent.

capability: Order statuses: the stages an order is set to, which the merchant can customize (Salla Order statuses / حالات الطلب, تخصيص حالات الطلب, Order Status, order.status.updated)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (/orders/statuses, SA-S-1775). Homonym: Shopify's order-status targets (customer-account.order-status.*) are the buyer's order status page in the customer account, not statuses an order is set to (domain D's CM-CUS-014); they are not cited.

capability: Order cancellation (Salla Order cancellation / إلغاء طلب, order.cancelled; Shopify Orders > Cancel, CANCEL_ORDERS, orders/cancelled)
note: Salla gives it a settings page of its own (orders/cancellation, SA-S-1745) and a concern (SA-C-046); Shopify keeps it in SH-C-054 (M-023's granularity), with a staff permission and a webhook topic of its own. Under CM-ORD-001 by both: Shopify's permission is Orders > Cancel; Salla's setting is under orders.

capability: Orders the merchant creates: draft orders and manual orders (Shopify Draft orders, Drafts, Create order; Salla إنشاء طلب يدوي, order_create / إضافة طلب)
note: A join on role, a reading: Shopify's route titled Create order is its draft orders' new route (draftOrders:new, SH-S-7094), and Salla's plan line is إنشاء طلب يدوي, create a manual order (SA-S-1989), with the staff permission order_create (SA-S-2273). Whether Salla's manual order passes through a draft stage, and whether Shopify's drafts serve quotes, isn't stated. Salla's price-quote status (طلب عرض سعر) is domain D's CM-B2B-004. Under CM-ORD-001: Shopify's route is in its section Orders; Salla's plan line is in its group إدارة الطلبات (adar-altlbat).

capability: Order risk and fraud analysis: the platform flags orders that may be fraudulent for the merchant to review (Shopify Built-in fraud analysis, Risk, orders/risk_assessment_changed; Salla نظام الحماية من الاحتيال)
note: No parent: Shopify's help places fraud analysis under managing orders (SH-S-0747), while Salla's plan line sits in its payment group (aldfaa, SA-S-1971). Salla's side is SA-C-122, which scope.tsv gives the PAY area's batch to land (notes). Domain D's CM-CUS-006 holds Salla's tag عميل غير جاد, which rests on the same anti-fraud system (SA-S-5052).

capability: Order assignment to staff (Salla Order Assignment, Auto assignment / إسناد الطلبات تلقائيًا للموظفين)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (/orders/auto-assignee, SA-S-1777). Not Shopify's order routing, which assigns orders to fulfillment locations (SH-C-060, the SHP area).

capability: Order invoices: the invoice the store issues and prints for an order (Salla Order Invoice, Invoice settings / إعداد إصدار فواتير الطلبات, طباعة فاتورة الطلب; Shopify Invoice and receipt apps)
note: A join on role, a reading (U-019): Salla's invoice settings at /orders/invoice-settings and its Order Invoice API, against Shopify's App Store category Invoice and receipt apps, which "offer additional document types" (SH-S-7225). Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping. Homonym: Shopify's draft orders "send invoices" (SH-S-7225), a draft order's invoice to the buyer, not an issued sales invoice. ZATCA e-invoicing is split from SA-C-044 and is the TAX area's.

capability: Packing slips and other printed order documents (Shopify packing slip template, document templates; Salla طباعة ملخص الطلب, order-summary)
note: No parent: Shopify places its packing slip and document template routes in its section Shipping (SH-S-7100, SH-S-7101), and Salla's print order summary sits in its group إدارة الطلبات (SA-S-1988). The SHP area's batch may want it under a fulfilment capability. The admin print action (admin_print), through which apps print documents, is domain F's CM-APP-008. Parent CM-SHP-001 (the coordinator, after batch 11, by convention 6): Shopify's packing slip routes sit in its admin section Shipping (SH-S-7100); Salla's print order summary is a plan line in its order-management group (SA-S-1988), not an admin grouping, so no grouping is shared and Shopify's admin grouping decides.

capability: Order receiving settings: whether, when and how many orders the store accepts, and how a placed order is confirmed (Salla Accept orders / استقبال الطلبات, Ordering hours, daily order limit / تعيين الحد اليومي للطلبات, Order acknowledgment, Set orders as "Completed" upon placement, Order confirmation page)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (orders/processing/..., SA-S-1736). Salla's daily order limit is not Shopify's Order limit apps (U-084, apart): what those apps limit isn't stated, and batch 1 cites them in CM-CHK-005.

capability: Order tags and automatic tagging (Salla Auto tags, order-auto-tagging)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (/orders/auto-tags, SA-S-1789). Shopify's automations that tag orders, if any, would be domain F's CM-AUT-001 (Flow); none is cited here.

capability: Deleting orders, and deleted orders kept for restoring (Salla Deleted orders, order_delete, restore-data; Shopify Orders > Delete, DELETE_ORDERS, orders/delete)
note: Salla gives deleted orders a link of its own (/orders/trash, SA-S-1892). Under CM-ORD-001 by both: Shopify's permission is Orders > Delete; Salla's link is under orders. Shopify's statements show deletion, not a store of deleted orders.

capability: Notes and comments on an order (Salla Customer notes, إضافة تعليق على الطلب, order-comment)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (orders/customer-notes, SA-S-1744). Salla's customer notes and its order comment are held together: neither is defined apart from the other, and both are notes on one order.

capability: Reorder: repeating a past order (Salla Reorder, تكرار الطلب, order-reorder)
note: Only Salla shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Salla's grouping (orders/reorder, SA-S-1746). Not domain D's CM-LOY-007, reminders to buy again, nor D's CM-B2B-005, a business buyer's saved lists. Who repeats the order, the buyer or the merchant, isn't stated.

capability: Payment methods and providers: the store's payment settings, where the merchant activates the providers and methods its buyers pay with at checkout (Shopify Payments settings, Payment providers; Salla Payments, Payment methods / طرق الدفع)
note: The root of the area's tree. Q1's M-025 joins Shopify's Payments settings page (SH-C-062) and payments apps (SH-C-076) with Salla's external gateways (SA-C-120), and its own granularity note puts Salla's Payments settings page in SA-C-110: a difference of grain, so the settings page is this parent and each kind of provider or method is a child. The later PAY batches add the children for third-party providers, wallets, instalments, manual methods and the rest.

capability: The platform's own payment service: online payments processed through the platform itself (Shopify Payments; Salla Payments / مدفوعات سلة, المدفوعات الإلكترونية)
note: Q1's M-026, joined on both platforms' definitions. Under CM-PAY-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route payments:settings:shopify-payments sits in its payments settings (SH-S-5248), and Salla's Salla Payments is activated from its Payment methods tab (طرق الدفع, SA-S-0051) at /payments. The service's own parts (onboarding, processing behind it, payouts, fees) are its children. Its payment methods (Salla's mada, cards, Apple Pay, STC Pay; Shopify's Shop Pay and local methods) are left to the later PAY batches.

capability: Payment service onboarding and verification: the checks a store passes before it can take payments through the platform's service, its KYC and underwriting (Shopify Payments Verification and Underwriting, KYC, read_financial_kyc_information; Salla Store Verification / توثيق المتجر, /payments/kyc, kyc_new_workflow)
note: Q1's M-003. Under CM-PAY-002 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's checks are those of the Payment Services (SH-S-0132); Salla's Store Verification link is /payments/kyc (SA-S-1881) and verification opens the way to e-payments (SA-S-0137). Not domain A's CM-TRU-002, identity verification of the people behind a store, which cites Shopify's profile-assessment route and ProfileAssessment section as core under SH-C-008's keys; they are cited here only as shows. Salla's verification also serves e-commerce registration rules (domain A's CM-TRU-010).

capability: Processing, acquiring and holding funds behind the platform's payment service: the payment processors, acquirers and licensed entities that process and settle its transactions and hold the merchant's funds (Shopify Payment Processor, Financial Services Provider, Payment Facilitator, Acquirer, Regulated Payment Services; Salla عقد خدمات الدفع)
note: A grain chosen here: Shopify holds four concerns (processing and settlement, SH-C-064; custody of funds, SH-C-065; payment facilitation in the EU/EEA and UK, SH-C-066; regulated payment services in Canada, SH-C-067), all in the Shopify Payments Terms of Service and its Payment Processor List, with no admin place of their own. Q1's U-027 asks the same question of all of them against Salla's SA-C-114 and SA-C-177: who processes, holds the funds and under which licence. One capability holds them; each scope stays its statement's. Shopify gives it pages of its own: the Payment Processor List (www.shopify.com/legal/processor-list) and the regional terms.

capability: Payouts: the payment service's balance of the merchant's sales, paid out to the merchant's bank account on a schedule (Shopify Payouts, payout schedule, Shopify Payments payouts; Salla رصيد المدفوعات الإلكترونية, دورة تحويل المدفوعات الإلكترونية, list_epayments)
note: Q1's M-027. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's payouts are Shopify Payments payouts (read_shopify_payments_payouts, View Shopify Payments payouts); Salla's e-payments balance holds what its e-payments collect (SA-S-0076). Not domain A's CM-PLN-006, Salla's prepaid store balance: Salla says the two balances differ (SA-S-0079, SA-S-0083). Not domain F's CM-PTN-003, the platform's payouts to partners. The payout bank account stays here: Shopify keeps it in SH-C-069 (read_shopify_payments_bank_accounts, bank account requirements); Salla splits it into SA-C-112.

capability: Reserves and payout holds: funds the payment service holds back from the merchant's payouts for a time (Shopify Reserves, Reserve Account, account holds)
note: Q1's M-028 (Shopify and WooCommerce). Under CM-PAY-005 by Shopify's grouping: Q1 places SH-C-070's where on its Payouts route, payments/payouts (SH-S-6325). Only Shopify shows it so far.

capability: Payment processing fees of the platform's payment service: the rates charged on the transactions it processes (Shopify Payments rates, Shopify Payments Fees, Payment rates; Salla رسوم المدفوعات الإلكترونية, حاسبة رسوم المدفوعات الإلكترونية)
note: Q1's M-029. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's routes Shopify Payments Fees and Payment rates sit in its Payments section (SH-S-7104, SH-S-7105); Salla's fees are those of its e-payments, set by the payment services contract (SA-S-0082). Not domain A's CM-PLN-003, the platform's fee on sales through other providers (Shopify's third-party transaction fees, Salla's platform commission).

capability: Payment terms: an order paid after it is placed, on terms and a payment schedule the merchant sets (Shopify Payment terms, payment schedules, Set payment terms)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-ORD-001 by Shopify's admin grouping: its staff permissions Set payment terms sit in the categories ORDERS and DRAFT_ORDERS (SH-S-7152, SH-S-7153). Shopify's API reference lists it among its B2B resources (SH-I-0004), but no statement held limits payment terms to business buyers, so it isn't domain D's CM-B2B-001. Homonym: Salla's تعيين شروط الدفع عند الاستلام (SA-S-2027) is cash on delivery's conditions, not payment terms on an order.

capability: Chargebacks and disputes: a buyer's bank or card issuer disputes a payment, and the merchant contests it (Shopify Disputes, Chargebacks and inquiries, Manage disputes, disputes/create)
note: Q1's M-030 (WooCommerce's WC-C-116). Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's API groups disputes in its Shopify Payments resources (SH-I-0024) with the scopes read_shopify_payments_disputes and dispute evidences, and its Shopify Payments Terms hold them in Part I, C. Contesting Chargebacks and Disputes (SH-S-0115); the admin route sits in its section Finances (risk/disputes, SH-S-7107). Not domain A's CM-TRU-020 or D's CM-SUP-008, which are buyers' complaints about a store, nor Salla's Transactions reverse (SA-C-123), a reversal the merchant makes.

capability: Chargeback protection: the platform covers the merchant against fraudulent and unrecognized chargebacks on eligible orders paid through its payment service (Shopify Protect)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify Protect "is offered as an add-on to the general Shopify Payments services" (SH-S-0402) and its route shopify-protect sits in the section Payments (SH-S-7108). Not CM-ORD-006, order risk and fraud analysis, which flags orders for the merchant to review: Shopify Protect evaluates orders too (SH-S-0404), but what it gives is cover for the chargeback. Not CM-PAY-009, the disputes themselves.

capability: Third-party payment providers and gateways: a provider other than the platform's own service that the merchant connects to take payments (Shopify Third-party payment providers, payments apps, Payments Apps API; Salla بوابات الدفع الأخرى, its external gateways)
note: The finer side of Q1's M-025: Shopify's SH-C-076 and Salla's SA-C-120 (whose batch lands it). Under CM-PAY-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route Third-party payment providers sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7114), and Salla's other gateways are reached from its Payment methods page (SA-S-0069). Shopify's providers come as apps on its Payments Apps API; Salla's are integrations it names, each switched by a flag.

capability: Digital wallets: third-party wallets the buyer pays with (Shopify Apple Pay, Google Pay, Meta Pay, Amazon Pay; Salla المحافظ الرقمية, Apple Pay, Google Pay, stc pay)
note: Q1's U-023. Under CM-PAY-001: Shopify creates the wallets' accounts "for you to accept payments" (SH-S-0024); Salla's wallets are plan lines in its payment group (parent_code aldfaa) and PayPal is chosen from its page طرق الدفع (SA-S-0199). Salla's Apple Pay and Google Pay come through Salla Payments (SA-C-110). The wallets also give accelerated checkout buttons, which CM-CHK-008 holds (SH-S-0419).

capability: PayPal as a payment method (Shopify PayPal Express Checkout, PayPal Wallet; Salla PayPal الدفع عبر)
note: Q1's M-032. Under CM-PAY-012 by the grouping both platforms share: Shopify's plan row is PayPal Wallet rates (SH-S-7024), and Salla says PayPal is available as a digital wallet option (يتوفر PayPal كخيار للمحفظة الرقمية, SA-S-0199). Q1's granularity note: Salla's concern also holds stc pay direct and Mokafaa Al Rajhi, which aren't PayPal. Batch 7 lands Salla's SA-C-119 in the parent CM-PAY-012, as coarser than PayPal (the coordinator).

capability: Saved buyer checkout details: the platform saves the buyer's payment method and address so that checkout goes faster (Shop Pay; Salla حفظ بطاقة وعنوان العميل)
note: Q1's U-026. Under CM-CHK-008 by Shopify's grouping: its Shop Pay Merchant Terms put Shop Pay under "1. Accelerated Checkout (Shop Pay)" (SH-S-0413), and Shopify says accelerated checkouts "save customer payment and shipping information" (SH-S-7287, cited in CM-CHK-008). Shopify's admin route for it sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7111), and Shop Pay "only enables payment processing through the sharing of payment credentials" (SH-S-0408), so the area is PAY. Salla's side is a join on role, a reading: its shopping experience fee includes the services of saving the customer's card and address (SA-S-0104). Whether Salla's saved details serve the buyer in other stores isn't stated.

capability: Instalments and buy now, pay later: the buyer pays for an order later or in instalments (Shopify Shop Pay Installments; Salla وسائل الدفع الآجلة, الدفع بالتقسيط عبر تابي وتمارا)
note: Q1's M-031. Under CM-PAY-001 by both platforms' grouping: Shopify's route shop-pay-installments sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7112); Salla's deferred payment methods are a section of its payment methods page (SA-S-0070). Shopify's is offered under a Merchant Agreement with Affirm (SH-S-0126); Salla's are providers it names (Tabby, Tamara and others). Homonym: Salla's الدفع الآجل here is buy now pay later, not CM-PAY-008's payment terms.

capability: Manual payment methods: methods paid outside the online payment flow, such as cash on delivery and bank transfer (Shopify Manual payment methods, Record payments, Mark as paid; Salla الدفع عند الاستلام / Cash on delivery, التحويل البنكي)
note: Q1's M-033, a difference of grain: Shopify keeps these methods in one concern (SH-C-079), while Salla splits cash on delivery by who collects it (SA-C-115 through Salla's shipping labels, SA-C-116 through the merchant's own carrier) and keeps bank transfer apart (SA-C-117). The Salla batches may add children for them. Joined by definition: Shopify names "manual payment methods such as cash, cash on delivery (COD), and bank transfers" (SH-S-0322). Under CM-PAY-001: Shopify's route Manual payment methods sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7117); Salla's cash on delivery setting sits under shipping (shipping/shipping.cod, SA-S-1765) and its bank accounts under its payment methods (SA-S-0095). Batch 7 adds its children CM-PAY-029, cash on delivery, and CM-PAY-030, bank transfer (the coordinator).

capability: Local payment methods: region-specific ways to pay, offered through the platform's payment service (Shopify Local payment methods, Accept local payment methods*, managed payment methods; Salla KNET through مدفوعات سلة for Kuwait stores)
note: Q1's U-024. Under CM-PAY-002: Shopify's are activated "with Shopify Payments" (SH-S-0420) under its route shopify-payments:local-payment-methods; Salla's KNET "is available through Salla Payments for Kuwait stores" (SA-S-0065). Salla's side is a join on role, a reading: Salla doesn't call KNET local; its statement scopes it to Kuwait's stores. Salla's KNET through Tap (SA-S-0130) is a gateway, in CM-PAY-011.

capability: Cryptocurrency and stablecoin payments (Shopify cryptocurrency gateways, USDC rates, Cryptocurrency Payment Protocol)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far, and Q1's U-025 holds only WooCommerce on the other side. Under CM-PAY-001: Shopify places it on its Payments settings (settings/payments, SH-S-6328), through third-party cryptocurrency gateways (SH-S-0428) and through Shopify Payments in eligible regions (SH-S-0433). Shopify's Cryptocurrency Credit Reward Program pays some credits in stablecoins (SH-S-0434); that is shows here.

capability: Payment method rules: conditions that hide, reorder or restrict the payment methods a buyer is offered at checkout (Shopify Payment customizations, the Payment Customization function; Salla Payment restrictions / قيود الدفع)
note: Q1's U-022, a join on role, a reading: Shopify's function can "rename, reorder, hide the payment methods available to customers during checkout" (SH-S-0589); Salla's payment restrictions are "conditions imposed on payment options", such as restricting a payment method for some countries or customers (SA-S-5050). Under CM-PAY-001 by the grouping both share: Shopify's route Payment customizations sits in its section Payments (SH-S-7119), Salla's link Payment restrictions at /payments/rules (SA-S-1877). Salla gives fraud as the reason; Shopify's statements give none (Q1 gap). Shopify lists it among its Function APIs as well; batch 1's function capabilities (CM-CHK-005, -006) have no parent, but this one's admin route and Salla's both sit in payments.

capability: Payment transactions on an order: authorizing, capturing and recording an order's payments, and acting on a transaction afterwards (Shopify order transactions, Payment authorization and capture, Capture payments; Salla Transactions / عمليات الدفع الإلكتروني)
note: Q1's M-034, one-to-one by the term transactions: Shopify's concern covers authorization and capture (SH-C-084), Salla's the refund, void and reverse of a transaction (SA-C-123). Both give it a place of its own: Shopify's webhook topics order_transactions/create and tender_transactions/create and its staff permission Orders > Capture payments; Salla's link Transactions at /payments/transactions (SA-S-1880), its API folder Transactions and its scope transactions. Parent CM-ORD-001 by Shopify's admin grouping: its where is the Orders page (SH-S-6322) and its permissions sit under Orders and Drafts. Salla's grouping differs: its link sits in the payments list (/payments/transactions) and its permission payments_operations_management in the group إعدادات المتجر, while its refund permission order_refund_payment sits in the group الطلبات (see notes). The refund itself is RET's: Salla's refund permission is shows here.

capability: In-person card payments: card payments the buyer makes at the point of sale, processed through the platform's payment service or a provider (Shopify In-person card rates, Shopify Payments for POS, card_present_payments, Tap to Pay; Salla الدفع بالبطاقة في كاشير سلة بوينت, SoftPOS)
note: The payment's processing, its rates and its rules, not the point of sale or its devices: domain E holds the point of sale (CM-POS-001) and its card-present devices (CM-POS-002), whose note leaves the card payment's processing and rates to domain C (SH-C-086). Shopify gives it a place of its own: the plan rows In-person card rates and In-person manual rates (SH-S-7027, SH-S-7029) and the billing category Tap to Pay transaction fees (SH-I-1352). Q1's M-036 joins SH-C-086 with WooCommerce's WC-C-014; no Salla concern of domain C holds it, and Salla's side is SA-C-095's (domain E, which names C under also for its Geidea card-present payment statements). Under CM-PAY-001, the grouping the two share, a reading: Shopify's in-person payments run through Shopify Payments (SH-S-0436, SH-S-0047), Salla's through Geidea (SA-S-5040), so CM-PAY-002, the platform's own service, would fit Shopify's side only.

capability: Saved customer payment methods and payment mandates: payment methods the store keeps for a customer and charges for later orders without the customer going through checkout (Shopify customer payment methods, payment mandates, Charge vaulted payment method)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far; Q1's M-035 holds it with WooCommerce's payment tokens (WC-C-098, WC-C-042). Its own place: the customer's route Payment methods (SH-S-7120), the scopes read_customer_payment_methods, read_payment_mandate and write_payment_mandate, the webhook topics customer_payment_methods/create, /update and /revoke and the staff permissions Orders > Charge vaulted payment method and PAY_ORDERS_BY_VAULTED_CARD. Not CM-PAY-014, saved buyer checkout details, a reading: Shop Pay saves the buyer's details "making the checkout process faster" (SH-S-0406), while these are stored to pay for future orders "without requiring the customer to manually go through checkout" (SH-S-0592), charged by the store. No parent: Shopify's route sits on the customer's record (section Customers, domain D's) and its permissions under Orders and Drafts; neither is a capability of this area. Salla's flag checkout-save-cards (SA-S-3123, SA-C-110) saves cards at checkout and is left to the Salla batches for CM-PAY-014 (notes).

capability: The merchant's money account with the platform: a business account in the admin that receives the store's sales and holds and spends the merchant's money (Shopify Balance, Banking)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin section Banking (SH-S-1547), the routes shopify-balance/* and access_account/shopify-balance, the plan row Manage money with Shopify Balance (SH-S-7062) and the staff permission View Balance account activity (SH-S-7168). Not A's CM-PLN-006, Salla's prepaid store balance with the platform, spent on the platform's services, nor D's CM-LOY-001, the buyer's wallet with the store, nor CM-PAY-005, the payment service's payouts, which may be paid into it (SH-S-0347). No parent: Shopify's own grouping puts it in its Finance suite (SH-S-0454) beside Shopify Credit and Shopify Capital (CM-PAY-025, CM-PAY-026), not in Settings > Payments; no capability holds the Finance suite as such (notes). Parent of CM-PAY-024.

capability: Business cards on the merchant's money account: payment cards the merchant spends its account's money with (Shopify Balance Visa® Commercial cards, Cards)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin route finance/cards (SH-S-5098) and the section Cards (SH-S-1552). Under CM-PAY-023 by Shopify's own name, Shopify Balance Visa® Commercial cards, and its rule that personal use of the card may end the Shopify Balance account (SH-S-0465). Q1 split it from the account because the card's issuer (Celtic Bank) differs from the account's funds holder. The route's unlock also takes the permission MANAGE_ALL_SHOPIFY_CREDIT_CARDS (SH-S-5099), Shopify Credit's (CM-PAY-025).

capability: Business credit for the merchant: a charge card with a credit limit, issued to the merchant and paid in full or repaid from its sales (Shopify Credit, Shopify Credit pay-in-full Visa® card)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin section Credit (SH-S-1559), the routes credit and access_account/credit, the plan row Shopify Credit pay-in-full Visa® card (SH-S-7064) and the staff permission View all Shopify Credit account activity (SH-S-7169). Not CM-PAY-026: Shopify Credit is a card account with a credit limit set by the issuing bank (SH-S-7267), while Capital is funding repaid from a share of sales. Shopify Credit's Program Terms are an agreement with Shopify Capital Inc. (SH-S-7276), a company of Shopify's group by its name; whether that company offers Capital isn't stated in the statements held. Not CM-PAY-024: Credit has its own section and route, apart from Cards. No parent, as for CM-PAY-023.

capability: Merchant financing repaid from sales: funding the platform offers or arranges for the merchant, as a loan or a merchant cash advance, repaid from a share of the store's sales (Shopify Capital; Salla capital / financial-support, صندوق سلة)
note: Q1's M-038, a difference of grain: Shopify splits Shopify Capital by country, because the lender differs (SH-C-091 to SH-C-097), Salla keeps one concern (SA-C-128). One capability holds all seven Shopify concerns, each statement keeping its country scope: they share one admin section Capital (SH-S-1551), one route access_account/capital, one entitlement shopifyFinance.capital and one plan row, and differ only by lender and agreement, which are slot fillers. Both define it as financing repaid from sales: Shopify's loan repayments "from a daily percentage rate of your daily sales" (SH-S-0482), Salla's collection of 25% of net sales from each payment (SA-S-0111). Both give it a place: Shopify's section Capital and plan row Flexible growth funding through Shopify Capital (SH-S-7063); Salla's flag financial-support, released on the Pro and Special plans (SA-S-3487), and its dashboard's capital.* texts. No parent, as for CM-PAY-023.

capability: Paying the merchant's bills to its vendors: the merchant schedules and pays its business bills from the platform (Shopify Bill Pay)
note: Only Shopify shows it so far. Its own place: the admin routes finance:billpay and finance:billpay:redirect, gated by the feature canAccessBillPay and the entitlement shopifyFinance.billPay (SH-S-5166, SH-S-5167), and the plan row Schedule, pay, and manage bills with Shopify Bill Pay (SH-S-7065). Bills are paid "using a bank account or your Shopify Balance account" (SH-S-0501), so it is not a child of CM-PAY-023: the money account is one source of payment among others. No parent, as for CM-PAY-023, -025 and -026, the other parts of Shopify's Finance pages. Not A's CM-PLN-005 (paying the platform's bills) nor CM-PLN-004: these are the merchant's own bills to its vendors. "Bills" is a homonym (notes, batch 6).

capability: Accounting and ERP integrations: connecting the store's sales and finances to an accounting system or an ERP (Shopify Accounting apps, ERP apps; Salla Accounting & Finance / المحاسبة والمالية, ERP system, الربط مع الخدمات المحاسبية)
note: Q1's M-077, one-to-one. Both give it a place of its own as an app category: Shopify's App Store categories Accounting apps and ERP apps (SH-S-2706, SH-S-2613), Salla's app categories Accounting & Finance and ERP system (SA-S-1194, SA-S-1195, SA-S-1222). Salla also gives it plan lines (الربط مع الخدمات المحاسبية, سلة برو) and released flags for named accounting services. Area PAY by the seed's "balance and finances"; scope.tsv names G under also for both concerns. No parent: neither platform groups it under its payment settings.

capability: Cash on delivery: the buyer pays in cash when the order is delivered, and the amount reaches the merchant through the platform or directly from the carrier (Salla الدفع عند الاستلام / Cash on delivery, through بوليصات سلة or the merchant's own carrier; Shopify cash on delivery (COD), a manual payment method)
note: Q1's M-033, a difference of grain: Salla gives cash on delivery a place of its own, its setting Cash on delivery (shipping/shipping.cod, SA-S-1765) and its plan lines الدفع عند الاستلام and تعيين شروط الدفع عند الاستلام, and splits it by who collects (SA-C-115 through Salla's shipping labels, SA-C-116 through the merchant's own carrier). One capability holds both: the split is who collects and settles, which the cells' placements show (core where Salla transfers the balance from its labels' carriers, SA-S-0122; outside where the carrier settles with the merchant, SA-S-0120, SA-S-0121). Under CM-PAY-016 by Shopify's grouping, which names cash on delivery among its manual payment methods (SH-S-0322); Salla's setting sits under shipping. Homonym: Salla's cash-on-delivery balance in its wallet (SA-S-0106) is not the e-payments balance of CM-PAY-005.

capability: Bank transfer as a payment method: the buyer pays by transfer to a bank account the store shows at checkout (Salla التحويل البنكي, bank_accounts_management / إدارة الحسابات البنكية, نظام المدفوعات الفورية عبر سريع; Shopify bank transfers, a manual payment method)
note: Q1's M-033, a difference of grain: Salla keeps bank transfer apart (SA-C-117) and gives it plan lines and a staff permission of its own (SA-S-1956, SA-S-1957, SA-S-2435). Under CM-PAY-016 by Shopify's grouping (SH-S-0322). Homonym: this bank account, shown to customers at checkout (SA-S-0095), is not the payout account of CM-PAY-005 (SA-C-112), which Salla's help says isn't shown to them.

capability: Amounts withheld from the merchant's wallet for app partners: an app the merchant installs has the platform hold an amount of the merchant's balance and settle it with the partner (Salla Settlements / إدارة المبالغ المحجوزة, Create Instant Settlement, managed settlement)
note: Salla gives it a place of its own: the Merchant API folder Settlements and the access scope settlements (إدارة المبالغ المحجوزة), whose instant-settlement endpoint is allowed only for dropshipping applications (SA-S-0179). Salla's shipping apps' managed settlement (SA-C-145, SA-S-5065, SA-S-5066) withholds label amounts from the wallet the same way, a reading. Homonym: this settlement, between the merchant and an app partner, is not the payment processors' settlement of transactions (CM-PAY-004).
